question: A 35-year-old Indian man has a BMI of 24 kg/m² and a waist circumference of 92 cm. How would you classify him using Asian-Indian cut-offs?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. BMI 24 kg/m² is in the overweight range for Asian-Indians (≥23 kg/m²), not normal weight (≤22.9 kg/m²).
Correct! Asian-Indian cut-offs: overweight ≥23 kg/m² (his BMI = 24), and abdominal obesity in men ≥90 cm (his waist = 92 cm). Both criteria are met.
Incorrect. Asian-Indian obesity threshold is ≥25 kg/m², so BMI 24 is overweight, not obese. The waist circumference of 92 cm exceeds the male cut-off of 90 cm.
Incorrect. BMI 24 kg/m² exceeds the Asian-Indian overweight threshold of ≥23 kg/m², so weight classification is overweight, not normal.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review Asian-Indian BMI cut-offs: overweight ≥23 kg/m², obese ≥25 kg/m²; abdominal obesity: men ≥90 cm, women ≥80 cm waist circumference.
Well done. Remember: Asian-Indian overweight ≥23, obese ≥25; waist cut-offs men ≥90 cm, women ≥80 cm — all lower than Western WHO thresholds.
